title: Lists and tables: col, dl, ol and thead drawn by a canvas
blurb: Five canvases that each hold a real table or list: a light that follows the pointer along a <col>, a <dl> as cards that turn over, an <ol> whose items enter one after another, a sticky <thead> that casts a shadow, and an <ol> drawn along a curve with its own markers as the numbers.
question: Which parts of a table or list can a canvas use on their own: the box of a <col>, a <dt> and its <dd>, a list marker, a sticky header inside a scroll container?
result: A <col> has a box and no picture. An outside list marker isn't in the picture of its <li>, an inside one is, and a source-rectangle draw of the <ol> has both. A drawable scroll container scrolls natively inside the canvas and raises paint on every step.
